# Volume 3 — Chapter XXII Spring and Nell Return to Grey Shutters

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Flickering across the kitchen walls of Grey Shutters went the shadows cast by the hearthfire, since coolness marked the spring evening; entering by the unclosed eastern window came the delicate, pleasing sounds of the dark hours. Thirza sat beside the hearth—physically, that is. Mentally, her youthful feet carried her through paths of the past. Recently, Thirza had passed numerous hours in this fashion, despite believing she ought to be crafting knitwear for the twins.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0000 }

“I guess I am getting older,” she remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0001 }

Still, Thirza was scarcely altered over those nine years, except for having become somewhat skinnier, and still more sharp-featured; a few additional gray strands showed in her hair, which remained coiled into that very same tight bun, pinned through by two hairpins—could those be the exact same hairpins? Her look, however, had transformed immensely; that quality around her lips that used to suggest a capacity for humor was now remarkably pronounced; the expression in her eyes was softer and kinder, while she smiled with greater frequency and gentleness.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0002 }

Thirza reflected upon the entirety of her past existence, from her restricted yet contented early years, to the secret dreams and crushed aspirations of her youth, and then the enduring, drab, restricted, unvarying period of uninteresting middle age. Afterwards came the arrival of Nell—a bright, creative, passionate youngster possessing a loving heart and a realm of imagination, who brought along hue, heat, and brilliance, transforming the barren expanse of life into something flourishing like a rose. It seemed to Thirza that among her sixty years of life, the only ones she had truly experienced were the nine that came after Nell's appearance. Furthermore, Nell was returning home the next evening.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0003 }

Opening, the kitchen door revealed a figure, and Thirza raised her eyes anticipating Mrs. Sowerby. Instead, Nell was standing in front of her, height impressive and eyes gleaming like stars, while holding an abundance of Mayflowers and violets.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0004 }

“Nell Harcourt!” Thirza cried out. Just this once, her customary restraint abandoned her; she embraced her girl, pressing her and her blossoms tightly to her chest, affectionately kissing her radiant hair and lovely face. “I didn’t expect you until tomorrow evening. By what means did you travel from Delford?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0005 }

“I came on foot, most beloved Thirza. Did I not accomplish this twenty times during the Regent’s era? My luggage will be delivered by the mailman tomorrow; a sudden wave of longing for home simply overtook me, so my arrival was moved up by a day. And ah! That stroll through the May dusk was so wonderful; I paused beside the barrens to gather these Mayflowers; my path led through Violet-Vale, which currently resembles a giant bowl filled with violets—those precious, sky-colored blossoms. Inhale their scent, Thirza—absorb them fully.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0006 }

Thirza dutifully took a sniff, yet her curiosity lay far more with Nell than with the aroma of violets.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0007 }

“Take a seat, child. You have to be completely exhausted. I’ll go fetch some dinner for you.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0008 }

“A lovely moon is coming up past the hills this evening, Thirza, and oh, the frogs serenaded me all the way from Delford! The music of the frogs is something I truly love. It appears tied to every one of my fondest memories of past spring nights. And I am always reminded by it of my very first evening here. Is it something you recall, Thirza?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0009 }

“Indeed, I am,” Thirza replied emphatically, “for it is hardly probable that I will at any point forget it.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0010 }

“That year, their singing in the brook and the marsh was so wild. From my window during the dusk, I would hear them and ponder how their song could appear simultaneously so joyful and so mournful. Oh, returning home feels truly wonderful! Although Wexcombe was magnificent and Harborough was charming, home is Grey Shutters.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0011 }

“From what I gather, Hugh won't be returning home this summer,” Thirza remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0012 }

“No.” Nell spoke in a voice that caused Thirza to look at her abruptly, yet Nell seemed completely focused on setting her violets inside a bowl. “Look, aren’t they sweet?” she continued with haste. “The year resembles a book, doesn't it, Thirza? Mayflowers and violets write the pages of spring, roses write summer's, red maple leaves write autumn's, and holly and evergreen write winter's.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0013 }

“Was Hugh successful in his exams?” Thirza continued to ask.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0014 }

“Splendidly. He was at the top of his class. But where have the twins and Mrs. Sowerby gone?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0015 }

“Agatha and Lucy are visiting Mr. Pettifer’s house. Robin has gone down to Boulters’. Right now, I believe I can hear him approaching.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0016 }

Robin charged inside, caught sight of Nell, halted, and thereupon threw himself at her with a happy cry.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0017 }

“Oh, Nell, seeing you makes me so happy! Listen, Nell, since previous autumn my height has increased by two inches. My measurement was taken by Mrs. Sowerby using her tape today, and listen, Nell, look at my front tooth. I don't have it anymore. After Mrs. Sowerby fastened a piece of string's first end onto it, she attached the opposite end to the door and subsequently closed the door. Two cents were paid to me by Milty when I sold it to him. Teeth are being collected by Milty.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0018 }

“Why on earth does he need teeth?” Thirza inquired.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0019 }

“For a necklace to play Indian Chief,” Robin explained, scrambling onto Nell’s lap. “Fifteen are already in his possession, and all the others have been promised, meaning it is pointless for any of the remaining group to begin gathering them as well. The Boulters are exceptional at business, I am telling you.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0020 }

“Did you behave well while at Mrs. Gammon’s?” Thirza demanded sternly.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0021 }

“Indeed; however listen, Thirza, being good has grown exhausting to me.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0022 }

“You would grow weary of misbehaving far more quickly, Robin-boy,” Nell remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0023 }

“Well, it would be enjoyable for the duration, wouldn't it?” Robin insisted. “Afterward, I could regret it, couldn't I?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0024 }

“Feeling regret could not eliminate the results of misbehaving, Robin. Have you forgotten that Sunday a year ago in the summer time when you fled from Sunday School? At that time, you mentioned to me that doing wrong was not beneficial. What activity were you and Milty engaged in this afternoon?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0025 }

“Well, we went fishing and pursued the cat, and searched for eggs, and shouted at the echo. A tremendous echo exists in the bush behind the Gammon barn. Tell me, what is echo, Nell; I wish to know.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0026 }

“Echo, Robin, is a lovely nymph who resides far off in the forest and chuckles at everyone from amidst the hills.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0027 }

“How is she described?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0028 }

“Darkness marks her hair and eyes, yet white as snow describes her neck and arms. The full extent of her beauty remains hidden from every mortal eye. She possesses greater fleetness than a deer, and our knowledge of her is limited solely to that mocking voice of hers. Nighttime brings the sound of her calling; beneath the stars, the sound of her laughter can be heard. Yet she remains forever invisible to you. Should you pursue her, she flies to a distance, continuously laughing at you from just beyond the adjacent hill.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0029 }

“Is that factual, Nell? Or is it a lie?” inquired Robin, gazing intently.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0030 }

“Robin,” Nell asked in desperation, “do you not possess sufficient sense to tell a fairytale apart from a lie?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0031 }

“Robin persisted, “I want to know what it is, then, that talks back from the Gammon bush?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0032 }

“I will clarify everything for you, Robin, once you have grown somewhat older.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0033 }

Robin’s thoughts were clearly redirected by the reference to age, as following a brief pause for consideration, he uttered in a low, earnest voice:
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0034 }

“Nell, I am about to get married.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0035 }

“At what time?” Nell inquired, matching the previous gravity.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0036 }

“Oh, naturally not before I have reached adulthood.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0037 }

“Well, that brings some ease, Robin. Who might the lady be?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0038 }

“Mabel Fletcher; we attend the same class at school. Also, listen, Nell, no girl you have ever laid eyes on is prettier than she is. Should my death occur prior to my reaching adulthood, you will watch over her, will you not?”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0039 }

“Robin Farrow, you must cease speaking such absurdity,” Thirza remarked sternly.
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0040 }

“It is not nonsense,” Robin objected, sounding hurt. “She is betrothed to me, and if I were to pass away, she would be my betrothed widow, would she not? And nobody else exists to take care of her besides her elderly grandmother.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0041 }

“Nell, approach to consume your evening meal,” Thirza uttered, “and avoid promoting the boy's foolish speech.”
{: #nw-v03-c22-p0042 }
